# 7. Files

Files live on the Ultimate's drives (SD card, USB sticks, its RAM disk
`/Temp`) and, with an REU, on the MOS's own RAM disk `/REU`. Paths are
the Ultimate's: `/SD/games/elite`, or relative to the current directory
(`*DIR`).

## 7.1 The filing system

#### `FILES`

Files are kept on the Ultimate's own storage: USB sticks (/Usb0, /Usb1), the SD card (/SD) and the RAM disk (/Temp, gone after power off). Names are Ultimate paths, relative to the current directory.

```
*DIR /Usb0/bbc    choose a directory
*CAT              list it
SAVE "game"       save the program
LOAD "game"       load it again
CHAIN "game"      load and run
```

Two files can be open at the same time (channels &11 and &12): OPENIN, OPENOUT, OPENUP, BGET#, BPUT#, PRINT#, INPUT#, PTR#, EXT#, EOF#, CLOSE#.

Programs are saved in the BBC's tokenised format, so programs from BBC Micro disc images can be loaded once extracted to a file.

See also: *CAT, *DIR, *LOAD, *SAVE, *TYPE, *DELETE, *RENAME, *MKDIR.

#### `/REU` (also `RAMDISK`, `RAM`)

The REU RAM disk: up to 127 files in the REU from 1 MB up (an REU of 2 MB or more), as the directory /REU. *DIR /REU makes it current (*DIR .. goes back), or give names as /REU/NAME.

LOAD, SAVE, CHAIN, *LOAD, *SAVE, *CAT, *DELETE, *RENAME and *TYPE work there at REU speed, as do OPENIN, OPENOUT, OPENUP, BGET#, BPUT#, PTR#, EXT# and EOF#. *COPY copies between /REU and the Ultimate's drives:

```
*COPY GAME /REU
*COPY /REU/GAME /Usb0/games
```

Names up to 16 characters, no directories. The disk survives a reset, not switching off.


## 7.2 Directories and files

#### `*CAT` (also `*.`)

```
*CAT     (also *.)
```

Lists the current directory: the path, then the files in two columns. Directories end in /. ESCAPE stops the listing.

#### `*DIR` (also `*CD`, `CD`)

```
*DIR <path>     (also *CD)
*DIR ~
```

Changes the current directory. Paths are Ultimate paths: /Usb0/bbc, /SD, /Temp, .. for the parent; ~ is the Ultimate's home directory (User Interface settings).

```
*DIR /Temp
*DIR ..
```

#### `*PWD`

```
*PWD
```

Prints the current directory.

#### `*MKDIR` (also `*CDIR`, `CDIR`)

```
*MKDIR <name>   (also *CDIR)
```

Creates a directory.

#### `*DELETE`

```
*DELETE <name>
```

Deletes a file.

#### `*RENAME`

```
*RENAME <old> <new>
```

Renames a file.

#### `*COPY`

```
*COPY <file> <directory>
```

Copies a file into another directory on the Ultimate's storage, under the same name. An existing file there is not overwritten (error "File exists").

```
*COPY game /USB0/backup
```

#### `*TYPE`

```
*TYPE <name>
```

Prints a text file. Lines end in CR; LF and other control codes are skipped. ESCAPE stops.

#### `*LOAD`

```
*LOAD <name> <address>
```

Loads a file into memory at an address (decimal or &hex), between &1D00 (&900 with *SOUND NONE) and &7FFF.

```
*LOAD screen &3000
```

#### `*SAVE`

```
*SAVE <name> <start> <end>
*SAVE <name> <start> +<length>
```

Saves memory to a file. The end address is not saved. Memory up to &7FFF can be saved.

```
*SAVE code &3000 +&200
```

#### `*INFO`

```
*INFO <name>
```

Shows a file as DFS does: name, L if locked, load and execution address, length (hexadecimal). Files on the Ultimate's drives have no addresses (0).

#### `*ACCESS`

```
*ACCESS <name> L   lock
*ACCESS <name>     unlock
```

Locks a file on the RAM disk (/REU): a locked file cannot be deleted, replaced, renamed or opened for output ("Locked"). The Ultimate's drives have no lock: their files give an error.

#### `*DUMP`

```
*DUMP <name>
```

Shows a file in hexadecimal: the offset, 8 bytes and the same bytes as characters (. for control codes). ESCAPE stops.

#### `*RUN`

```
*RUN <name>
```

Loads machine code and calls it. A file with a load address (*SAVE on /REU) goes there and is called at its execution address. Otherwise the file is a C64 program file: its first two bytes are the load address, and it is called there. Only &0400-&7FFF.

#### `*SPOOL`

```
*SPOOL <name>   start
*SPOOL          end
```

Copies everything printed into a file, as on a BBC Micro: *SPOOL name, then for example LIST, then *SPOOL alone. The output is collected in the REU's last 64K (up to 47K) and written to the file when the spool ends (also by CLOSE#0 or another *SPOOL), so it is fast and safe while the MOS prints during file operations. Needs an REU; the RAM disk ends below the REU's last 128K (this 64K and *MAP's).

```
*SPOOL listing
LIST
*SPOOL
```

#### `*EXEC`

```
*EXEC <name>
```

Reads the file as if it were typed: every byte becomes a key, at the prompt and in programs (GET, INKEY, INPUT), until the file ends; *EXEC alone or ESCAPE stops it. LF ends a line too (files from a PC). A program typed in as text can be loaded this way, or a list of commands run.

```
*EXEC commands
```

#### `*BUILD`

```
*BUILD <name>
```

Writes the lines you type into a file, each ended by CR, until ESCAPE. The line numbers shown are not written. Made for *EXEC files.


## 7.3 Files from programs: channels

Two files can be open at the same time. `OPENIN` reads, `OPENOUT`
creates, `OPENUP` reads and writes; all return a channel number (0 when
the file cannot be opened).

#### `OPENIN`

```
c=OPENIN "name"
```

Opens a file for reading; 0 if it cannot be opened. See FILES.

#### `OPENOUT`

```
c=OPENOUT "name"
```

Creates a file (or empties an existing one) for writing.

#### `OPENUP`

```
c=OPENUP "name"
```

Opens an existing file for reading and writing; 0 if it cannot be opened.

#### `BGET#` (also `BGET`)

```
b=BGET#c
```

Reads one byte from channel c. See FILES.

#### `BPUT#` (also `BPUT`)

```
BPUT#c,b
```

Writes byte b to channel c.

#### `PRINT#`

```
PRINT#c,v[,v...]
```

Writes values to channel c, typed, for INPUT#.

#### `INPUT#`

```
INPUT#c,v[,v...]
```

Reads values written by PRINT#c.

#### `PTR#` (also `PTR`)

```
PTR#c
PTR#c=n
```

The position in the file on channel c; can be set.

#### `EXT#` (also `EXT`)

```
EXT#c
```

The length of the file on channel c.

#### `EOF#` (also `EOF`)

```
EOF#c
```

TRUE at the end of the file on channel c.

#### `CLOSE#` (also `CLOSE`)

```
CLOSE#c
```

Closes channel c; CLOSE#0 closes all channels.


## 7.4 Data in the REU

Programs can keep data in the REU, from &40000 up (the MOS uses the
first 256K):

#### `*SRWRITE`

```
*SRWRITE <start> <end> <REU addr>
*SRWRITE <start> +<len> <REU addr>
```

Copies memory to the REU, as the BBC Master's sideways RAM command. Programs keep data there (tables, levels, text, pictures) and fetch it with *SRREAD. REU addresses &40000-&8FFFF (320K; above them the Upic picture, *UPIC, the snapshots, *SNAPSHOT, and from &100000 the RAM disk); memory from PAGE to &7FFF. Numbers decimal or &hex.

```
*SRWRITE &3000 +&1000 &40000
```

OSWORD &42 does the same from a program (see OSWORD).

#### `*SRREAD`

```
*SRREAD <start> <end> <REU addr>
*SRREAD <start> +<len> <REU addr>
```

Copies from the REU into memory at start, the reverse of *SRWRITE.

```
*SRREAD &3000 +&1000 &40000
```
